absent: Exact numeric values of conditional VM event identifiers and zone expansion spellings under each configuration.
Formatting sink, concurrency rules and storage source for crash info appends.
Core notification delivery, filter evaluation and identifier-based removal semantics beyond the inline wrappers.
Windowed extremum update algorithm beyond reading and resetting.
XZ decoder call sequence, memory handling and recovery from each reported outcome.
ZSTD functional entry points, parameter ranges and streaming behavior beyond type aliases and constants.
Codec behavior that consumes the deflate window and memory tunables.
Pipe interaction, note lifecycle and permission checks for watch queues.

findings.text: Virtual memory accounting defines an extensive event identifier set covering paging, swapping, per-zone allocation and stall behavior, reclaim scanning, compaction, migration, huge pages, ballooning, TLB flushing, swap and compressed swap, direct-map splits, lock statistics and stack usage, terminated by a count sentinel that gives the table size.
File huge-page accounting provides failing placeholders when the feature is unavailable, so any use triggers a build-time failure while still yielding a zero value to keep expressions well formed.

Crash note geometry uses aligned header, name and descriptor extents summed into a total byte count, while crash info reserves a full page and defines a fixed note name with aligned header accounting for its own note size.
Crash note storage is a word array sized as one quarter of the total crash note byte count, giving aligned 32-bit access to the note area.

Crash info recording offers labeled emitters for release string, build identity, page size, symbol addresses, object and structure sizes, field offsets, array lengths, numeric values and configuration flags.
Build identity emission expects a twenty-byte vector and validates that width at compile time before formatting it as hexadecimal text.
Hardware error source reporting is an empty inline entry that accepts a source discriminator and performs no observable action.
Per-type notification selection carries a type discriminator plus a subtype bitmask and a masked info comparison pair for filtering.
Aggregate notification filter overlays reclamation state with an accepted-type bitmap and stores a filter count plus a flexible array of per-type entries sized by that count.

Notification queue bundles reclamation state, a protected filter pointer, an optional pipe buffer that is absent when closed, a head of contributing watches, preallocated note pages with allocation bitmap and size counts, a usage reference and a serialization lock.

Single watch object combines reclamation or identifier state, a queue pointer, queue and list linkage nodes, a watched-list pointer, owner credentials, private object data, an internal identifier and a usage reference.
Watched-object list holds reclamation state, a head of current watchers, a callback invoked to release a detached watch and a serialization lock.
Watched-list mutation is serialized by its embedded lock; initialization prepares an empty watcher head, initializes the lock and stores the release callback.

Notification posting forwards to the core path only when a list is present, carrying notification data with credentials and identifier; list removal detaches by identifier and then reclaims the list after a grace period.
Notification length derivation scales an object size by a fixed left shift defined for the info length field.
Fallback queue creation always reports unavailable package support, so callers must handle queue setup as unsupported in this build.
Windowed extremum tracking stores three timestamped samples, each pairing a measurement time with its observed value.
Reading the tracker yields the current extremum value; resetting replicates one fresh timestamped measurement into all slots and yields that value.
Word utilities provide upper-half and lower-half extraction for narrow portions, replication of a byte pattern across a full word, and truncation of that replicated pattern to 32 bits.
Byte mask formation has two build-selected variants, one generating a low mask from a byte count and the other generating a high mask from word width and byte index.

Compressed stream handling distinguishes single-call, preallocated and dynamic allocation modes and reports progress, normal termination and seven distinct failure classes for checks, memory, limits, format, options, data and buffer conditions.
Stream buffers describe input and output separately with base pointers plus current offsets and total extents, allowing incremental consumption and production.
Internal checksum selection is a build-switched binary flag with disabled and enabled alternatives.
Deflate tuning fixes an upper memory level and an upper window exponent for a large history window, with default window and memory choices derived from those upper bounds.
Portability aliases define a narrow byte type, two progressively wider unsigned integer types and a generic untyped pointer.

Kernel compression interface re-exports upstream contexts, dictionaries, streams, buffers, parameters, strategies and sequence helpers under simplified lowercase aliases without altering their abstract roles.

Error reporting enumerates stable failures from success and generic errors through prefix, version, frame, corruption, dictionary, parameter, table, stage, memory and buffer problems, plus higher unstable extension codes and a terminal maximum marker that must never be used directly.

Library versioning identifies a fixed major, minor and release triple with combined numeric and string forms, defines frame and dictionary markers plus a skippable-frame range with mask, caps block sizing by a logarithmic limit, and reserves all-ones patterns for unknown versus erroneous content sizes.

Input limits adapt to address width with separate wide and narrow ceilings, and the worst-case output bound adds proportional overhead plus a small-input margin while preserving subadditivity for large inputs.
Compression and decompression contexts appear only as opaque forward declarations, hiding all internal state from callers.

Decompression advances by repeated calls that consume input and fill output until normal termination; check, memory, format, options, data and buffer reports act as terminal or corrective signals rather than forward progress.

Strategy selection orders nine strengths from fastest to strongest with only ordering guaranteed, while detailed compression controls use numeric selectors for level and for window, hash and chain sizing with documented ranges and defaults.
Queue content and note allocation are guarded by the queue lock, while filter replacement and watch linkage rely on deferred reclamation for concurrent readers.
Symbol visibility defaults to empty with a hidden-attribute alternative, deprecation marking has build-selected empty or attribute forms, and the default compression level is a small fixed value.
